questions.question_text: Regarding common factors of psychotherapy, all of the following statements are correct, except:

options.text: The therapeutic relationship is the most important of the common factors of psychotherapy
Intense and rapid emotional release is called abreaction
Empathetic listening and providing information are important components of all forms of psychotherapy
In all forms of psychological treatment, reasons for the patient's condition should be provided indirectly through questions and interpretations
All psychological treatments contain an element of suggestion

correct_answer.text: In all forms of psychological treatment, reasons for the patient's condition should be provided indirectly through questions and interpretations

correct_answers.text: In all forms of psychological treatment, reasons for the patient's condition should be provided indirectly through questions and interpretations

questions.explanation: The reasons for the patient's condition may be stated directly by the therapist, as in short-term therapy, or indirectly through questions and interpretations, as in long-term therapy. With the exception of hypnosis, suggestion is not deliberately increased in psychological treatments; however, all psychological treatments contain an element of suggestion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true of transference?

options.text: It becomes increasingly strong as treatment progresses
Patients usually transfer feelings and attitudes from their relationship with their parents to the therapist
When transferred feelings are good, transference is said to be positive
It may lead to behaviour such as threats of suicide
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: If transference is interpreted and addressed appropriately early on, it may be helpful for patients to understand the true origins of their feelings and behaviour not only for the therapist but more widely.

questions.question_text: Regarding counselling, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: In the client-centred approach, counsellors take a passive role
Problem-solving counselling is a highly structured form of counselling
In interpersonal counselling, the therapist encourages patients to consider alternative ways of coping with their difficulties
In psychodynamic counselling, the patient's emotional reactions to the counsellor are considered as a source of information about problems in other relationships
Evidence from clinical trials indicates that debriefing improves the outcome of survivors of disasters

correct_answer.text: Evidence from clinical trials indicates that debriefing improves the outcome of survivors of disasters

correct_answers.text: Evidence from clinical trials indicates that debriefing improves the outcome of survivors of disasters

questions.explanation: Evidence from clinical trials indicates that debriefing does not improve the outcome of survivors of disasters, and methods using cognitive techniques may be more helpful.

questions.question_text: In grief counselling:

options.text: It is helpful to forewarn a bereaved person about unusual experiences such as feeling as if the dead person were present
The bereaved person should not be encouraged to view the body
Parents with a still-born baby should not be encouraged to name the dead baby
Parents with a still-born baby should not be encouraged to keep photographs of the body to look at later if they wish
If possible, the bereaved person should not be asked to put away the dead person's belongings

correct_answer.text: It is helpful to forewarn a bereaved person about unusual experiences such as feeling as if the dead person were present

correct_answers.text: It is helpful to forewarn a bereaved person about unusual experiences such as feeling as if the dead person were present

questions.explanation: Grief counselling helps the person to accept that the loss is real, to work through the stages of grief and to adjust to life without the deceased. The bereaved person's viewing of the body or putting away the dead person's belongings, or the parents of a still-born baby being encouraged to keep photographs of the body to look at later if they wish, helps this transition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true in relation to psychological therapies for abnormal grief?

options.text: Crisis intervention is not helpful
Brief dynamic therapy is more effective than a mutual support group
Group psychotherapy is significantly beneficial for bereaved spouses
There is evidence that it is helpful to provide psychotherapy for all bereaved persons
In a controlled evaluation, guided mourning produced modest benefit

correct_answer.text: In a controlled evaluation, guided mourning produced modest benefit

correct_answers.text: In a controlled evaluation, guided mourning produced modest benefit

questions.explanation: There is some evidence that crisis intervention may be helpful for people at high risk of an abnormal grief reaction (Raphael 1977); brief dynamic therapy is no more effective than a mutual support group (Marmar et al. 1988); group psychotherapy is no more effective than no treatment in bereaved spouses (Lieberman & Yalom 1992); in a controlled evaluation, guided mourning produced modest benefit (Clark 2004; Foa & Rothbaum 1997).

questions.question_text: Regarding psychological therapies for late effects of childhood sexual abuse, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Dynamic approaches focus on understanding the effects of the trauma on self-esteem and emotional expressions
Cognitive behavioural approaches emphasize how the current patterns of thinking affect the present behaviour
Group therapy is contraindicated
Various therapy methods allow patients to set the pace at which they talk about the experience of being abused
The therapist should take special care not to suggest memories of sexual abuse

correct_answer.text: Group therapy is contraindicated

correct_answers.text: Group therapy is contraindicated

questions.explanation: The late effects of childhood sexual abuse have been treated with counselling, dynamic psychotherapy, cognitive therapy and group therapy.

questions.question_text: Regarding recovered memories and false memories in relation to sexual abuse in childhood, which of the following is true?

options.text: Many victims have partial amnesia for the most stressful parts of the experience
Complete amnesia for repeated stressful events followed by their recall is frequent
There is evidence that memories of single non-abusive childhood events can be implanted by suggestion in 50% of subjects
Clinicians have reported that up to 80% of memories recovered in therapy are confirmed by other evidence
Clinical reports suggest that about 75% of patients reporting childhood sexual abuse describe long periods in which they did not remember the abuse

correct_answer.text: Many victims have partial amnesia for the most stressful parts of the experience

correct_answers.text: Many victims have partial amnesia for the most stressful parts of the experience

questions.explanation: Complete amnesia for repeated stressful events followed by their recall is less frequent and for many clinicians improbable. There is evidence that memories of single non-abusive childhood events can be implanted by suggestion in 25% of subjects (Brewin 2007; McNally 2003). Clinicians have reported that up to 40% of memories recovered in therapy are confirmed by other evidence. Some 25–50% of people reporting childhood sexual abuse describe long periods in which they did not remember the abuse.

questions.question_text: Caplan's description of stages of coping include all of the following, except:

options.text: Denial and disbelief
Emotional arousal with efforts to solve the problem
Greater arousal, leading to disorganization of behaviour
Trials of alternative ways of coping
Exhaustion and decompensation

correct_answer.text: Denial and disbelief

correct_answers.text: Denial and disbelief

questions.explanation: Denial and disbelief are the first stage of grief; btoeare the four stages of coping described by Caplan. Crisis intervention seeks to limit the reaction to the first stage or, if it has been passed before the person seeks help, to avoid the fourth stage.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true concerning supportive psychotherapy?

options.text: Opportunity should be given for repeated release of emotions
Reassurance should be offered in the first session
It is sometimes appropriate for doctors to use their powers of persuasion to help patients to take some necessary steps
Listening is not very important, as the therapy focuses more on information and advice
It is useful to direct dependence to the therapist rather than directing it to a group of staff members caring for the patient

correct_answer.text: It is sometimes appropriate for doctors to use their powers of persuasion to help patients to take some necessary steps

correct_answers.text: It is sometimes appropriate for doctors to use their powers of persuasion to help patients to take some necessary steps

questions.explanation: Supportive psychotherapy should not be attempted before using more active forms of psychotherapeutic interventions. Emotional release can be helpful in the early stages but repeated release is unlikely to be beneficial. Encouraging hope is important, but reassurance should be offered only when the patient's concerns have been fully understood. The therapeutic relationship, listening, information and advice, emotional release, encouraging hope and persuasion are important components of supportive psychotherapy.

questions.question_text: Several clinical trials have shown that interpersonal therapy is effective for:

options.text: Depressive disorders in adults
Depressive disorders in adolescents
Dysthymia
Bulimia nervosa
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Interpersonal therapy was shown to be effective in depressive disorders in adults and adolescents by Mufson et al. (2004) and in dysthymia by Markowitz (2003).

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about interpersonal therapy, except:

options.text: To deal with role disputes and role transitions, patients are helped to negotiate with the other person
Treatment is carried out mostly in an unstructured way
The initial assessment period lasts one to three sessions
Among interpersonal problems, bereavement and other loss are considered
Interpersonal deficits are discussed when analysing present relationship problems

correct_answer.text: Treatment is carried out mostly in an unstructured way

correct_answers.text: Treatment is carried out mostly in an unstructured way

questions.explanation: Treatment is highly structured and the content of treatment and sessions is planned carefully.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about cognitive behavioural therapy, except:

options.text: It is concerned with the ways the disorder developed in the past
It focuses on the factors maintaining the disorder
The patient takes an active part and the therapist is an expert advisor
Therapeutic procedures are presented as experiments
Treatment manuals ensure that different therapists use evidence-based procedures

correct_answer.text: It is concerned with the ways the disorder developed in the past

correct_answers.text: It is concerned with the ways the disorder developed in the past

questions.explanation: Cognitive behavioural therapy is not concerned with how the disorder has developed in the past, but focuses on the factors maintaining the disorder at the time of treatment. Behaviour therapy focuses on the factors that provoke the symptoms or abnormal behaviour. Cognitive therapy generally focuses on two kinds of abnormal thinking: intrusive thoughts and dysfunctional beliefs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a maintaining factor in the assessment for cognitive behavioural therapy?

options.text: Avoidance
Safety-seeking behaviours
Selective attention
The response of others
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: One of the most frequent maintaining factors is avoidance (phobic and anxiety disorders). Many behaviours are maintained by their consequences (the response of others); increased attention is another reinforcer of behaviour. Two kinds of abnormal thinking that act as maintaining factors include intrusive thoughts and dysfunctional beliefs and attitudes. Three factors are thought to maintain dysfunctional beliefs and attitudes: attending selectively, thinking illogically and safety-seeking behaviour.

questions.question_text: Regarding the maintaining factors identified in cognitive behavioural therapy, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Avoidance prevents the extinction of the anxiety response
Escape from the anxiety-provoking situation is followed by a fall in anxiety, which reinforces the phobic avoidance
Children's unacceptable behaviour is reduced if parents pay more attention to the behaviour
Intrusive thoughts provoke an immediate emotional reaction, usually of anxiety or depression
Dysfunctional beliefs and attitudes determine the way in which situations are perceived and interpreted

correct_answer.text: Children's unacceptable behaviour is reduced if parents pay more attention to the behaviour

correct_answers.text: Children's unacceptable behaviour is reduced if parents pay more attention to the behaviour

questions.explanation: Increased attention is a powerful reinforcer and children's unacceptable behaviour can be increased if parents pay more attention to the behaviour.

questions.question_text: Patients with social phobias attend more to the critical behaviour than to signs of approval. This is an example of:

options.text: Illogical thinking
Selective attention
Selective abstraction
All-or-nothing thinking
Personalization

correct_answer.text: Selective attention

correct_answers.text: Selective attention

questions.explanation: Selective attention is attending selectively to evidence that confirms dysfunctional beliefs and attitudes, and ignoring or discounting evidence that contradicts them. Examples of illogical thinking include overgeneralization, selective abstraction, personalization and all-or-none thinking.

questions.question_text: In cognitive behavioural therapy, laddering is:

options.text: A special form of interviewing
Used to construct a hierarchy
The same as flooding
Used in modelling
Given as homework

correct_answer.text: A special form of interviewing

correct_answers.text: A special form of interviewing

questions.explanation: Laddering is a special interviewing technique for use with patients who need help to become aware of and describe maladaptive beliefs. A series of questions is asked, each about the answer to the previous question.

questions.question_text: In cognitive behavioural therapy, all of the following statements are true about the formulation, except:

options.text: The formulation is guided by the cognitive model of the disorder
An excessively critical parent is considered as a background factor in the disorder
A behaviour carried out because the person believes that it reduces an immediate threat but which in the long term perpetuates the person's concerns is described as an avoidance behaviour
A diagram on paper is used to build up the formulation step by step
The formulation is modified as necessary as a result of discussion with the patient

correct_answer.text: A behaviour carried out because the person believes that it reduces an immediate threat but which in the long term perpetuates the person's concerns is described as an avoidance behaviour

correct_answers.text: A behaviour carried out because the person believes that it reduces an immediate threat but which in the long term perpetuates the person's concerns is described as an avoidance behaviour

questions.explanation: A behaviour carried out because the person believes that it reduces an immediate threat but in the long term perpetuates that person's concerns is described as safety-seeking behaviour, which is a maintaining factor.

questions.question_text: Regarding behavioural techniques, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Relaxation training is useful for stress-related disorders like initial insomnia and mild hypertension
Exposure is used to reduce avoidance behaviour in phobic disorders
The results of flooding have been shown to be better than desensitization, as it is an intensive form of exposure
Exposure with response prevention is a treatment of obsessive compulsive disorder
Thought stopping is a distraction technique used to treat obsessive compulsive disorder

correct_answer.text: The results of flooding have been shown to be better than desensitization, as it is an intensive form of exposure

correct_answers.text: The results of flooding have been shown to be better than desensitization, as it is an intensive form of exposure

questions.explanation: In flooding, patients enter the top of the hierarchy from the start. Many patients find it distressing and the results of flooding have not been shown to be more effective than desensitization; flooding is rarely used.

questions.question_text: In exposure with response prevention, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The therapist explains the rationale of the treatment
Patients may be faced with unexpected tasks
Modelling is used
Obsessional thoughts occurring without rituals are more difficult to treat
Habituation training is used

correct_answer.text: Patients may be faced with unexpected tasks

correct_answers.text: Patients may be faced with unexpected tasks

questions.explanation: Every task is agreed in advance and patients will never be faced with an unexpected task. Habituation training is a form of mental exposure treatment.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about contingency management are true, except:

options.text: It involves another person monitoring the behaviour
It includes identifying the stimuli and reinforcing them by recording events before and after the behaviour
It is never used alone in the treatment of substance abuse
It is used mainly in the treatment of people with learning disability
When applied to a group of patients living together, the arrangement is known as token economy

correct_answer.text: It is never used alone in the treatment of substance abuse

correct_answers.text: It is never used alone in the treatment of substance abuse

questions.explanation: Contingency management is used alone or as a part of a wider programme in the treatment of substance abuse.

questions.question_text: Regarding behavioural techniques, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Social skill training is not useful in chronic mental disorder
An enuresis alarm is not very successful with children under the age of 6
Biofeedback may be of some value when normal sensory information is lost in spinal injuries
In aversion therapy, negative reinforcement is used to suppress unwanted behaviour
Habit reversal is a complex procedure used to treat T ourette's syndrome

correct_answer.text: An enuresis alarm is not very successful with children under the age of 6

correct_answers.text: An enuresis alarm is not very successful with children under the age of 6

questions.explanation: An enuresis alarm is not very successful in children under the age of 6, children who are uncooperative or children with associated psychiatric disorders.

questions.question_text: Regarding the techniques used in cognitive restructuring, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Thought stopping is a distraction technique
Neutralizing involves rehearsing a reassuring response
The therapist produces evidence that contradicts the beliefs
The patient's responsibility can be reassessed by constructing a pie chart
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: These principles are used in cognitive restructuring in the treatment of anxiety disorders, depression, eating disorders and psychosis.

questions.question_text: Dialectic behavioural therapy:

options.text: Is delivered by a team of therapists and gives access by telephone to the therapist between sessions
Uses cognitive behavioural techniques, including self-monitoring
Uses the practice of detachment from experiences, known as mindfulness
Uses phrases that encapsulate the approach known as aphorisms
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Dialectic behavioural therapy was developed by Marsha M. Linehan as a treatment for patients with borderline personality disorder. Treatment is highly structured and intensive, with individual sessions, skills training in a group and access to the therapist by phone, and lasts up to one year.

questions.question_text: In cognitive analytical therapy:

options.text: Traps are repetitive cycles of behaviour in which the consequences of the behaviour perpetuate it
Dilemmas are false choices or unduly narrow options
Snags are the anticipation of highly negative consequences of actions
Scaffolding is the provision of just enough support to enable patients to discover their own solutions
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Cognitive analytical therapy was developed by Anthony Ryle; the theory of reciprocal roles was developed when it was applied to borderline personality disorder. According to Ryle, people's internalized templates can be abnormal in three ways: (1) the repertoire of different roles is restricted; (2) roles cannot be switched easily; and (3) roles are inflexible.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about psychodynamic interpersonal therapy, except:

options.text: It uses the patient–therapist relationship as a tool for understanding and changing interpersonal problems
It uses more interpretation of transference than do other kinds of psychodynamic therapies
The therapist uses metaphor to communicate with patients
It has been tested in clinical trials in people who deliberately self-harm
It has been tested in clinical trials in people with Alzheimer's disease

correct_answer.text: It uses more interpretation of transference than do other kinds of psychodynamic therapies

correct_answers.text: It uses more interpretation of transference than do other kinds of psychodynamic therapies

questions.explanation: Psychodynamic interpersonal therapy was developed by Hobson. It uses less interpretation of transference than do other kinds of psychodynamic therapies, and has been tested in clinical trials in high utilizers of psychiatric services (Guthrie et al. 1999), chronic functional dyspepsia (Hamilton et al. 2000), deliberate self-harm (Guthrie et al. 2001) and Alzheimer's disease (Burns et al. 2005).

questions.question_text: Regarding special techniques used in couple therapy, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Structural moves should not result in disagreement between partners
Reversed role-play is used to help the partners understand each other
In sculpting, partners take up positions, silently, to express some aspects of the relationship without words
Systemic tasks include making a timetable in which specific times are allocated for the interaction
Paradoxical injunctions are given as provocative statements designed to elicit a counter-response that the couple have previously resisted

correct_answer.text: Structural moves should not result in disagreement between partners

correct_answers.text: Structural moves should not result in disagreement between partners

questions.explanation: Structural moves include requiring disagreement, reversed role-play and sculpting. Couples may be asked to disagree about something when one partner dominates the other, who habitually gives in to avoid disagreement.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about family therapy, except:

options.text: It is used when young people living with their parents present with psychiatric problems
It is often combined with antidepressant therapy in adults presenting with depression
It is used in treating young people with anorexia after weight has been restored by other means, or who have a history of substance abuse or conduct disorder
It is contraindicated in schizophrenia
Circular questioning is often used to assess the family

correct_answer.text: It is contraindicated in schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: It is contraindicated in schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Special kinds of family treatment have been developed to reduce relapses in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Regarding treatment of personality disorders, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Psychological support is the mainstay of treatment, although medication should be considered as the first choice of treatment as it reduces hostility
The atypical antipsychotics olanzapine and risperidone have been reported to reduce the hostility and chronic dysphoria of borderline personality disorder
Fluoxetine is reported to be more effective than placebo in reducing anger in people with borderline personality disorder
A randomized trial of valproate reported beneficial effects in borderline personality disorder
Medications are generally better given to patients with borderline personality disorder than to those with dependence

correct_answer.text: Psychological support is the mainstay of treatment, although medication should be considered as the first choice of treatment as it reduces hostility

correct_answers.text: Psychological support is the mainstay of treatment, although medication should be considered as the first choice of treatment as it reduces hostility

questions.explanation: Medication should not be the first choice and when it is prescribed it should be part of a wider plan covering psychological and social needs.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), except:

options.text: Neurobiological studies suggest that hippocampal dysfunction prevents adequate memory processing
Cognitive theories suggest that PTSD arises when the normal processing of emotionally charged information is overwhelmed and the memories persist in an unprocessed form
Meta-analyses concluded that cognitive behavioural therapy is no more effective than inactive controls in terms of therapeutic effect size
Treatment trials using eye-movement desensitization reprocessing have shown similar effect sizes to those obtained with cognitive behavioural therapy
Meta-analysis carried out by the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) indicated that drug treatment has a smaller effect size than structured psychotherapy

correct_answer.text: Meta-analyses concluded that cognitive behavioural therapy is no more effective than inactive controls in terms of therapeutic effect size

correct_answers.text: Meta-analyses concluded that cognitive behavioural therapy is no more effective than inactive controls in terms of therapeutic effect size

questions.explanation: A meta-analysis suggested that CBT has a therapeutic effect size of 1.65 compared with inactive controls.

questions.question_text: Regarding anxiety disorders, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Cognitive behavioural therapy produces more improvement than no treatment in generalized anxiety disorder
The main treatment for specific phobia is SSRI antidepressants in the long term and benzodiazepines in the short term
Cognitive behavioural therapy is the psychological treatment of choice for social phobia, although SSRIs are often the first choice of treatment
Clinical trials indicate that, in the short term, cognitive therapy is about as effective as medication and in the long term it is probably more effective in agoraphobia
It was found that the combination of cognitive therapy and imipramine was no more effective in panic disorder than either treatment alone

correct_answer.text: The main treatment for specific phobia is SSRI antidepressants in the long term and benzodiazepines in the short term

correct_answers.text: The main treatment for specific phobia is SSRI antidepressants in the long term and benzodiazepines in the short term

questions.explanation: The main treatment for specific phobia is the exposure form of behavioural therapy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding obsessive compulsive disorder?

options.text: When given in high dose, clomipramine is more effective than placebo in reducing obsessional symptoms
There is some evidence to indicate that SSRIs are less effective than clomipramine
Exposure and response prevention result in substantial improvement in two-thirds of patients with moderately severe rituals
The immediate results of neurosurgery in severe cases are often a striking reduction in tension and distress
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Exposure and response prevention seems to produce better long-term results but it is difficult to achieve response prevention when symptoms are severe.

questions.question_text: Regarding conversion disorder, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Social factors appear to be major determinants of the onset and development of conversion symptoms
Some of the phenomena classified as conversion disorders in Western countries may in some other cultures be accepted as possession disorders
For acute conversion disorders seen in primary care or hospital emergency departments, reassurance and suggestion of improvement are appropriate
Antidepressants and cognitive behavioural therapy were found to be very effective in long-term management
Patients who do not improve should be reviewed thoroughly for undiscovered physical illness

correct_answer.text: Antidepressants and cognitive behavioural therapy were found to be very effective in long-term management

correct_answers.text: Antidepressants and cognitive behavioural therapy were found to be very effective in long-term management

questions.explanation: Medication has no direct role in the treatment unless the disorder is secondary to depressive or anxiety disorders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about the use of tricyclic antidepressants in the acute treatment of depression?

options.text: They are clearly more effective than placebo in all but the most severely depressed patients
They are more effective in patients with depressive psychosis
They are more effective in milder depressive states (i.e. those with Hamilton depression scores of less than about 14)
They are more effective with atypical depression
All of the above

correct_answer.text: They are clearly more effective than placebo in all but the most severely depressed patients

correct_answers.text: They are clearly more effective than placebo in all but the most severely depressed patients

questions.explanation: Tricyclics appear to be less effective in patients with depressive psychosis, milder depressive states (i.e. with Hamilton depression scores of less than about 14) and atypical depression.

questions.question_text: Regarding the treatment of depression, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: There is good evidence that cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than a waiting-list control condition

A review by the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) suggested that the combination of cognitive behaviour therapy with antidepressant medication was more effective than medication alone
There is sufficient evidence that cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than other psychotherapies
SSRIs are more effective than tricylics where depression occurs in association with obsessive compulsive disorder
Venlafaxine is little more effective than SSRIs in patients with more severe depressive states

correct_answer.text: There is sufficient evidence that cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than other psychotherapies

correct_answers.text: There is sufficient evidence that cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than other psychotherapies

questions.explanation: There is insufficient evidence that cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than other psychotherapies.

questions.question_text: Assessment for cognitive behavioural therapy in obsessive compulsive disorder requires all of the following, except:

options.text: Knowledge of the degree of family involvement
Knowledge of the patient's degree of insight or overvalued ideation
Assessment of the patient's readiness to change
Analysis of countertransference
Assessment of the patient's reasons for holding beliefs

correct_answer.text: Analysis of countertransference

correct_answers.text: Analysis of countertransference

questions.explanation: Analysis of countertransference is carried out only in dynamic therapies.

questions.question_text: Placebo-controlled studies of the role of continuation therapy in unipolar depression have reached the conclusion that:

options.text: Continuing antidepressant treatment for 6 months past the point of remission halves the relapse rate
Treatment should be at the originally effective dose if possible
In a working age population at low risk of relapse, continuation of antidepressant treatment for longer than 6 months confers little benefit
In elderly people at low risk of relapse, continuation of antidepressant treatment for 12 months is more appropriate
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: About a third of patients withdrawn from medication relapse over the next year, with the majority of relapses occurring in the first 6 months.

questions.question_text: Regarding the treatment of recurrent mood disorders, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Longer-term antidepressant maintenance treatment in recurrent depressive disorder reduces the relapse rate
The use of lithium in patients with recurrent mood disorders is associated with a significant reduction in mortality from suicide
Evidence supports the longer-term use of valproate in the maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder as it is more effective than lithium
Lamotrigine has a modest benefit in the prevention of mania and has a clearer prophylactic effect against depression
In the longer-term maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder, there is evidence that olanzapine is equivalent to lithium in overall efficacy

correct_answer.text: Evidence supports the longer-term use of valproate in the maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder as it is more effective than lithium

correct_answers.text: Evidence supports the longer-term use of valproate in the maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder as it is more effective than lithium

questions.explanation: At present, evidence supporting the longer-term use of valproate in the maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder is slender and less than that for lithium.

questions.question_text: Regarding the treatment of mood disorders, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Cognitive therapy in the acute stage of depression lessens the risk of subsequent relapse
There is research evidence that education about the early signs of relapse reduces the rate of manic illness in bipolar patients

Research in elderly depressed patients found that a combination of nortriptyline and interpersonal therapy was more effective than nortriptyline and clinical management in preventing depressive relapse over 3 years
The National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) recommends combining cognitive behaviour therapy and antidepressants in severe depression
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Cognitive therapy in the acute stage of depression lessens the risk of subsequent relapse.

questions.question_text: Effective psychosocial interventions for schizophrenia include:

options.text: Family therapy and psycho-education
Cognitive remediation
Social skills training
Assertive community treatment
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Cognitive behavioural therapy, supported employment, illness management skills and integrated treatment for comorbid substance abuse are other recognized psychosocial interventions.

questions.question_text: Regarding the treatment of schizophrenia, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Drug treatment has most effect on the positive symptoms
Many controlled trials have shown the effectiveness of continued antipsychotic therapy
Depot medications are more successful than continued oral medication in preventing relapse
In clozapine-resistant schizophrenia, there is strong evidence in favour of augmentation with lamotrigine or valproate
Family interventions with education have been shown to lower the rates of hospitalization and improve medication compliance

correct_answer.text: In clozapine-resistant schizophrenia, there is strong evidence in favour of augmentation with lamotrigine or valproate

correct_answers.text: In clozapine-resistant schizophrenia, there is strong evidence in favour of augmentation with lamotrigine or valproate

questions.explanation: In clozapine-resistant schizophrenia, there is only weak evidence in favour of augmentation with lamotrigine or valproate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of premature ejaculation?

options.text: It is more common in older men
It can be treated with the start–stop technique
It can be treated with the squeeze technique
It can be treated with the quiet-vagina technique
SSRIs can be useful in its treatment

correct_answer.text: It is more common in older men

correct_answers.text: It is more common in older men

questions.explanation: Premature ejaculation is more common in younger men, especially during their first sexual relationships.

questions.question_text: Regarding sexual dysfunction in men, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Primary cases of erectile disorder may occur through a low sexual drive and anxiety about sexual performance
Erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation are the most common sexual problems in men
Lack of sexual interest is the most common sexual problem in women
In sensate focus therapy, patients are strongly encouraged to check their own state of sexual arousal
Early studies suggested that sex therapy is successful in a third of patients

correct_answer.text: In sensate focus therapy, patients are strongly encouraged to check their own state of sexual arousal

correct_answers.text: In sensate focus therapy, patients are strongly encouraged to check their own state of sexual arousal

questions.explanation: Sensate focus therapy involves behavioural psychotherapy with graded assignments; patients are strongly discouraged from checking their own state of sexual arousal.

questions.question_text: Regarding the prognosis of obsessive compulsive disorder, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Two-thirds of cases improve to some extent within a year
Prognosis is better when there is a precipitating event
Prognosis is better when the symptoms are episodic
Prognosis is better when the onset is in childhood
Prognosis is worse when there is a personality disorder

correct_answer.text: Prognosis is better when the onset is in childhood

correct_answers.text: Prognosis is better when the onset is in childhood

questions.explanation: The prognosis is worse when onset is in childhood and when social and occupational adjustment is poor.

questions.question_text: Contraindications of brief insight-oriented therapy include:

options.text: Obsessional disorders
Hypochondriachal disorder
Severe mood disorder
Schizophrenia with past emotional problems causing present distress
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Brief insight-oriented therapy is also contraindicated in some personality disorders that lead to acting out.

questions.question_text: Electroconvulsive therapy causes all of the following, except:

options.text: Increased cerebral noradrenergic activity
Increased cerebral serotoninergic function
Increased cerebral tyrosine hydroxylase activity
Increased cerebral dopamine concentration
Increased cerebral acetylcholine concentration

correct_answer.text: Increased cerebral acetylcholine concentration

correct_answers.text: Increased cerebral acetylcholine concentration

questions.explanation: Electroconvulsive therapy causes decreased cerebral acetylcholine concentration and increased cerebral acetylcholinesterase activity.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about electroconvulsive therapy are true, except:

options.text: It is a rapid and effective treatment for depressive stupor
It may cause worsening of mania
It is useful in the treatment of acute catatonic states
It is effective for positive symptoms such as delusions and thought disorder in schizophrenia
It was found to be useful in people with intractable Parkinson's disease

correct_answer.text: It may cause worsening of mania

correct_answers.text: It may cause worsening of mania

questions.explanation: Electroconvulsive therapy can lead to a rapid resolution of mania but is generally reserved for patients who do not respond to drug treatment or for those whose manic illness is severe.

questions.question_text: When is there an increased suicidal risk in schizophrenia?

options.text: When there are frequent exacerbations of psychosis
When there is good premorbid functioning
Early in the course of the disorder
During hospitalization or shortly after discharge
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: In addition to the demographic risk factors associated with suicide in other psychiatric disorders, such as male gender, social isolation, unemployment, and previous suicidal behaviour, these are factors specific to schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: The psychological variables that may be associated with suicidal behaviour include:

options.text: Dichotomous thinking
Cognitive constriction
Problem-solving deficits
Overgeneralized autographical memory
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: All these could act by predisposing people to act impulsively.

questions.question_text: All of the following are recommended in the care of suicidal patients in hospital, except:

options.text: On admission, remove objects that might be used for suicide
Do not discuss the care plans with the patient as it may make suicidal attempts easier
Agree a visitor policy, including number of visitors, duration of visit and what they need to know
Agree a date of discharge and plan aftercare in advance
At discharge, prescribe in adequate but non-dangerous amounts

correct_answer.text: Do not discuss the care plans with the patient as it may make suicidal attempts easier

correct_answers.text: Do not discuss the care plans with the patient as it may make suicidal attempts easier

questions.explanation: Discussing and agreeing plans with the patient is recommended.

questions.question_text: Components of motivational interviewing include:

options.text: Expressing empathy
Detecting and rolling with resistance
Pointing out discrepancies in the history
Raising awareness about the contrast between substance users' aims and behaviour
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Motivational interviewing is used in alcohol misuse. This interview style, which avoids arguing and is not judgemental, can help to persuade the patient to engage in a useful review of his or her current pattern of drinking.
